questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: What Makes a State a State
questions.learningObjective: Define an altered state of consciousness
questions.stem: At the sports club, a coach asks what defines an altered state of consciousness.

options.text: A state differing from normal waking awareness
Any state of physical exercise
Only states caused by drugs
A state of complete unconsciousness only

questions.explanation: An altered state differs from normal waking awareness. It is not limited to exercise, drugs, or unconsciousness.

options.text: Alert, drowsy, sleep, coma is the only order
Coma, sleep, drowsy, alert is a plausible order
All states are equally responsive
Coma is more responsive than alertness

questions.explanation: Responsiveness increases from coma through sleep and drowsiness to alertness. The reverse or equal-responsiveness views misrepresent the continuum.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: Speaking and Moving in the First Part of the Night
questions.stem: A family asks how to keep a sleepwalking child safe.

answer.exemplar: Safety involves securing the environment, locking doors and windows, and gently guiding the walker back to bed without abrupt awakening.

questions.explanation: Environmental safety and gentle redirection help. Abrupt awakening can confuse or distress the sleeper.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: Acting Out a Dream and What It May Precede
questions.stem: A neurologist explains the significance of REM behavior disorder.

answer.exemplar: REM behavior disorder indicates loss of REM atonia and may signal future neurodegenerative disease, warranting long-term monitoring.

questions.explanation: RBD reflects failed REM atonia and may precede neurodegeneration. Monitoring is recommended.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: Irresistible Sleep and Sudden Loss of Tone
questions.stem: A patient asks what triggers cataplexy in narcolepsy.

answer.exemplar: Cataplexy is often triggered by strong emotions like laughter or surprise, causing sudden loss of muscle tone while consciousness remains.

questions.explanation: Strong emotions trigger cataplexy. Consciousness remains intact during the episode.

questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Sleep and Altered States: A Chemical Finding Behind Irresistible Sleep
questions.stem: A researcher synthesizes the role of hypocretin in sleep regulation.

answer.exemplar: Hypocretin promotes wakefulness and stabilizes sleep-wake transitions; its loss destabilizes these transitions, producing narcolepsy with sleep attacks and cataplexy.

questions.explanation: Hypocretin stabilizes wakefulness and transitions. Its loss destabilizes them, causing narcolepsy features.
